newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends thinly traded session higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends thinly traded session higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures posted moderate gains in extremely thin trading Friday as the market made a half-hearted attempt to bounce back from Thursday's tumble to three-month lows, dealers said.

After plummeting 15.35 cents -- or nearly nine percent -- Thursday, the benchmark September contract managed to close up 2.40 cents at 164.10 cents a lb after ranging between 165.50 and 160.75 cents. Spot July rose 3.50 cents to 186.00 cents, while outer months gained 1.00 to 2.40 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 21.90 cents compared with 20.80 cents at the close on Thursday, while the September/December switch held steady at 13.10 cents.

Arabica futures softened at the outset, pressured by some follow-through selling. However, September's ability to hold above chart support at 160.00 prompted locals and speculators to cover short positions, traders said.

They said steady buying of the forward contracts also helped bolster the market, with good trade interest noted in the December and March 1998 contracts near 150.00 cents and 140.00 censt respectively.

Some traders said market got a boost from the latest crop figures released on Friday by Colombia's National Coffee Growers Federation. The federation's latest estimate for total production for the 1996/97 coffee year is "about" 10 million bags, down from the 10.4 million bags forecast earlier in the year.
But Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said a lower Colombian crop was probably priced into the market and that the federation's production data for June could have been viewed as bearish.
Colombia's June coffee crop totaled 1.07 million 60-kg bags compared to 858,000 bags in the same month last year, the federation said.
"It's the first time they've met there target," said Ganes.
Ganes said, however, tight supply concerns are likely to re-emerge in the coming weeks ahead of the new-crop harvest in many Latin American countries this autumn.
But in the near-term, many market participants expect a build in certified coffee stocks and mild weather in top-producer Brazil to continue to weigh on sentiment.

CSCE reported after Friday's close that certified coffee inventories rose for the sixth day in a row, increasing by 4,486 60-kg bags as of July 10, to 70,601 bags. An additional 16,989 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
CSCE also reported that out of 11,666 bags graded only 2,520 bags passed exchange approval.

Traders await the monthly Green Coffee Association of New York's stock report for June. They expected the data, due out on Tuesday, July 15 at 1500 EDT, to be little changed. Preliminary forecasts for U.S. consumer coffee inventories in June have ranged from a decline of 100,000 bags to a build of 100,000 bags.
In May, GCA reported stocks of green coffee in U.S. warehouses rose by 122,000 bags, to 1,977,000 bags. Stocks in June 1996 fell by 110,000 bags, to 2,161,000 bags.
Technically, traders said September's ability to hold support at 160.00 gave some hope to diehard bulls. But some traders expected September to try and test the 155.00 or 150.00 support levels.
On the upside, they said September faced resistance at 165.00-165.50, with the next level seen near 168.00.
